title: Mila and the Moon
markdown:
The little cottage felt soft and warm, a cozy hug after a long stacking day. Mila the builder set one smooth stone on another, then another, making a tiny wall on the hearth rug. Pip the duck nestled in a basket of fluffy wool and made a small, pleased sound, the kind ducks make when they have decided not to waddle anywhere else.

Gran Ada watched from the chair. Her needles clicked a quiet song. Click, slip, click. The window held a dark garden and one big light.

Mila looked up. The moon sat in the sky like a soft pearl, round and pale. The world outside had gone quiet. No birds sang. Earlier, when the sun had been a gold coin over the hedge, Pip had fussed for a walk and Mila had stacked stones in the yard until Ada called them in for bread. Now the yard was silver instead of gold.

A gentle understanding bloomed, not a lesson spoken at anyone.

“The moon means night,” Mila whispered. “And the sun means day.”

Gran Ada chuckled softly, not waking the wool. “That’s right, Mila. The moon tells us to rest, and the sun tells us to play. They help us know when to be busy and when to snuggle down.”

Pip sighed. His eyes closed, then opened a slit, then closed again. Mila carefully took down her stones, one by one, and set them in a neat row so morning Mila would find them ready. She felt sleepy in her elbows first, then in her knees.

They looked at the gentle moon, a soft pearl in the quiet sky. A moth bumped the glass and thought better of it. Ada’s needles slowed.

Mila yawned a big, sleepy yawn. “It’s still night,” she whispered. “Time for sleeping.” She did not talk to a listener on the other side of the page. She tucked the last stone beside the others and pulled the wool up so Pip’s beak had a little cave.

Soon the cottage was filled with quiet breathing and soft dreams. The moon kept its post. The stones waited. Everything was just right, resting in the quiet night, with day promised on the other side of the hedge.
